name: Ghostwalk — race your old warehouse
one_liner: A browser-native 3D picking-floor twin that replays one real November of UCI Online Retail II orders (top-100 SKUs, ~2k invoices) with glowing self-drawing routes and heat-memory floors, lets the player re-slot cartons, then RACES a translucent ghost picker on the old layout against a solid picker on the new one on the exact same orders — while a fast-movers baseline and a simulated-annealing opponent set the bar; every number comes from one deterministic headless simulator with a time-split held-out set, zero backend, zero keys, static deploy.
why_it_wins:
1) It is the only one of the 12 statements where cinematic 3D IS a must-have (M2: "3D scene ... at least one animated picker ... live counters"), so every hour spent on bloom, camera choreography and instancing is an hour spent on requirements, not polish. All four scouts rank 4.2 first or second; judge-mindset scout estimates the lowest pick rate of the 12 (three.js scares ML students), so the field is empty.
2) The core challenge sentence ("scored by replaying exactly the same orders before and after, so the improvement is measured, not claimed") becomes the signature visual: the Ghost Race. The measurement is not a table the judge has to trust; it is two pickers on the same floor, same orders, counters diverging in front of them. Nobody else will render the evaluation as theatre.
3) Demo-safety is absolute: static Vite build on Vercel (+ Cloudflare Pages mirror + local `vite preview`), no LLM, no API key, no cold start, no rate limit, no venue Wi-Fi dependency after first load (fonts, GLB, JSON self-hosted). Same layout + same orders = identical numbers; judges can click Replay twice.
4) Technical depth that an OR/graphics expert respects and a student can explain line by line: aisle-graph all-pairs Dijkstra; exact Held-Karp DP per order (<=11 stops) with NN+2-opt+Or-opt fallback and an S-shape ablation; simulated-annealing slotting with incremental delta evaluation through an inverted SKU->orders index (captures order affinity that the ABC baseline cannot); Web-Worker scoring of the full month in tens of ms; time-split held-out evaluation with in-sample vs held-out gain reported.
5) Screenshot-ready by construction: safety-orange racks on dark concrete, cyan bloom route, heat-coloured cartons, two pickers, 48px counters — a single frame tells the whole story for the LinkedIn/X post.
Why not the alternatives from this lens: 4.3 has 25 synthetic points on a 2D map (an affine lie needing a banner), a Python solver backend with cold-start risk, and a ★★★ state model as the time sink; 3.3's 3D is only a stretch goal and That Open 3.x docs are thin; 2.3's visual is a grayscale 200x200 scatter. 4.2 lets us put 100% of the visual budget where the rubric already pays for it.
demo_script:
Pre-flight (T-10 min): open live URL once (assets cached), set Quality=High if the laptop holds 55+ fps in the built-in 5 s benchmark, else Auto; browser 125% zoom, notifications off; local `npm run preview` tab and MP4 backup open behind.

0:00-0:25 HOOK (title screen, camera parked high over the floor). Narrator: "In a warehouse, pickers walk more than they pick. This is a real month: November 2011, 2,0xx invoices from a UK gift wholesaler, UCI Online Retail II, CC BY 4.0. Every carton you see is one of the top-100 products, coloured by how often it was actually picked." Press Enter. WOW 1: 2.5 s intro dolly (CameraControls.setLookAt from (40,30,40) to a 3/4 isometric), racks glow in heat colours, dock hazard stripes, lamps bloom.

0:25-1:20 M2 REPLAY. Press Play. HUD left shows "Invoice 581xxx · 6 lines · 29 Nov 2011 14:32" and the line list with real descriptions ("WHITE HANGING HEART T-LIGHT HOLDER"). Camera drops to follow-cam behind the picker; the cyan route draws itself one segment ahead (WOW 2), next-stop ring pulses, metres and mm:ss tick live. Narrator: "Walking follows the aisle graph — no straight lines through racks. Routing per order is exact Held-Karp when the order has up to 11 stops." Click a carton: card shows StockCode, description, picks this month, slot id. Switch speed to 20x: orders stream, floor tiles accumulate heat memory (WOW 3), the chip reads "Animating 40 of 1,0xx held-out orders · full set scored headlessly in 38 ms".

1:20-2:00 M3 BASELINE. Camera lifts to Overview. Press "Baseline: fast movers nearest dock". WOW 4: 100 cartons fly in staggered parabolic arcs (15 ms stagger, 1.5 s cascade) to their new slots. KPI card fills: Original vs Baseline, total km and avg s/order, two columns "Optimise set Nov 1-15" and "Held-out Nov 16-30". Narrator says the held-out number out loud.

2:00-3:10 M3 GAME + WOW 5 (signature) GHOST RACE. In Overview, judge (or operator) clicks a carton (it lifts and glows) then clicks a target slot; the two cartons swap with an arc. Do 3-4 swaps guided by the affinity hint panel ("co-picked with 84 orders: 22423 REGENCY CAKESTAND 3 TIER — currently 31 m apart"). Press RACE. Two pickers leave the dock at once on the same order: the ghost (old layout, additive cyan, 35% opacity) and the solid orange picker (new layout). Dual counters diverge: "Ghost 2,184 m · You 1,730 m · -20.8%". Pause when the ghost is still in aisle 4 and the solid picker is back at the dock. Narrator: "Same orders, same routing rule, same speed. The gap is the measurement."

3:10-3:50 AI OPPONENT. Press "Let the annealer try" (Web Worker). WOW 6: energy curve falls in a sparkline while cartons shuffle in fast-forward (one arc per accepted swap, throttled to 60/s); temperature and iteration counter visible; seed shown. Final KPI row: AI (SA). Narrator: "In-sample gain X%, held-out gain Y% — smaller, as it should be. The annealer beats the ABC baseline because it puts co-picked products together; ABC cannot see that."

3:50-4:30 EVIDENCE PANEL (in-app, not slides). Split description, coverage chip ("top-100 SKUs cover Z% of November order lines; orders filtered to those lines"), parameters (1.2 m/s, 10 s per line, aisle 3 m, bay 1.2 m, dock front-left), routing ablation (S-shape vs exact DP on the same layout), `npm run eval` command and commit hash that produced `eval/results.md`. One breath of limitations: forward-pick area only, one picker, no congestion/batching unless stretch, synthetic layout, invoices treated as orders.

4:30-5:00 STRETCH + CLOSE. Toggle rack-visit heatmap; if done, show batch-picking row and two-picker congestion row in the KPI table; Leaderboard with "AI (SA)" as the fixed entry to beat; QR codes to live URL and repo. End on the Ghost Race frame.

Q&A cards ready (20 s each): how the headless score and animation share simulate(); why Held-Karp cutoff 11; how SA delta eval works; what "original layout" means; coverage honesty; why no backend; who owns which file.
wow_visual:
Palette (CSS tokens + three colours): floor #0b0f1a concrete, rack steel safety-orange #ff7a1a with #ffb067 highlights, cartons kraft #c9a66b lerped toward heat ramp (#1b2a49 -> #2fb3a8 -> #ffd166 -> #ff5a36), route cyan [0.2, 2.0, 3.0] (HDR >1 so Bloom catches it), ghost #8fd3ff additive 0.35, dock hazard #ffd400/#111. Fonts self-hosted in /public/fonts: Space Grotesk (UI), JetBrains Mono (counters; .woff copy for drei <Text>, troika cannot read woff2).

Scene graph (R3F 9.8.2 / drei 10.7.9 / three 0.186.1), draw-call budget <= 14 static:
- Floor: one plane 32x26 m, MeshStandardMaterial roughness 0.92 with a runtime CanvasTexture (2048x2048: concrete noise + painted aisle lines + bay numbers + dock stripes) — zero asset download.
- Racks: drei <Instances> for uprights (6 rack rows x 11 x 2 = 132 boxes 0.08x3.2x1.0), beams (6 x 10 x 3 levels x 2 = 360 boxes), and wire-deck shelves (one thin box per bay-level). Three InstancedMesh draw calls.
- Cartons: one <Instances limit={300}> (100 slots x 3 levels). Level 0 = pick face, instanceColor = heat ramp of pick frequency (or rack-visit heat when the toggle is on); levels 1-2 neutral reserve stock. A useFrame lerps current colour toward target colour at 6/s so re-colouring animates. Each carton has a small drei <Text> label (StockCode) rendered only within 12 m of the camera (distance-culled via one shared troika Text per visible bay, max 40 visible).
- Ceiling lamps: <Instances> of 15 emissive boxes (emissiveIntensity 4) hanging on thin rods: they bloom and give the "warehouse at night" look without an HDR download (no drei <Environment preset> — that fetches from a CDN; use <hemisphereLight> sky #3b4a6b ground #0b0f1a 0.6 + <directionalLight position [20,30,10] intensity 2.2 castShadow shadow-mapSize 2048 (High only)>).
- Picker: Kenney "Mini Characters 1" (CC0, https://kenney.nl/assets/mini-characters-1) GLB via useGLTF + useAnimations (walk clip timeScale proportional to replay speed), position evaluated per frame on the arc-length-parametrised polyline from the route reconstruction; yaw = travel direction; plus a procedural pick-cart (box + 4 cylinders, wheels spin). Fallback if the clip misbehaves: procedural capsule + cart (bob 2 Hz). Ghost = SkeletonUtils.clone of the same GLB with all materials replaced by MeshBasicMaterial({color:'#8fd3ff', transparent, opacity:0.35, depthWrite:false, blending:AdditiveBlending}).
- Route line: drei <Line points lineWidth={3} color={[0.2,2.0,3.0]} toneMapped={false}> for the segment already walked plus 3 m lookahead ("draws itself"); the remainder as <Line dashed dashSize 0.4 gapSize 0.3 color '#3a4a66'>; next stop = torus ring, scale pulsing 1 + 0.15 sin(6t), emissive cyan.
- Heat tiles: <Instances> of 66 aisle cells (each graph node) with a Float32Array of visit counts; colour = ramp(count/max) updated via setColorAt + instanceColor.needsUpdate once per animated order.
- Post (High only): @react-three/postprocessing 3.2.1 <EffectComposer multisampling={0}><Bloom luminanceThreshold={1} mipmapBlur intensity={0.7} radius={0.6}/><N8AO halfRes aoRadius={1.5} intensity={1.2}/> (n8ao 2.0.1, drop first if fps < 50) <Vignette offset={0.2} darkness={0.6}/><SMAA/></EffectComposer>. Low = no composer, no shadows, dpr 1. Auto mode: measure 90 frames after load; if median < 45 fps switch to Low; <PerformanceMonitor> from drei also lowers dpr between 1.5 and 1.
- Camera: drei <CameraControls smoothTime={0.6}> with four modes: intro() setLookAt(40,30,40 -> target 10,0,8, enableTransition) over 2.5 s; follow() per-frame setLookAt(px+6, 5, pz+6, px, 1, pz, true); overview() setLookAt(10, 38, 8.01, 10, 0, 8, true) with polar/azimuth locked; race() 3/4 isometric framing both pickers via fitToBox of their joint Box3 every 0.5 s. Click a carton -> fitToBox(rackBay, true) with padding.
- Swap/cascade animation: a 30-line tween list in useFrame: carton i moves along a parabola between slot positions (height 2.5 m, 380 ms, easeInOutCubic); baseline/SA application staggers tweens 15 ms apart; the annealer visualisation drains accepted swaps from the worker at <= 60/s.
- HUD (React, motion 14.5.0): order card left, 48 px JetBrains Mono counters (metres, mm:ss) animated with motion's animate(from,to,{duration:0.3,onUpdate}); race mode shows dual counters and a live delta bar; KPI card right with four rows (Original / Baseline / AI (SA) / You) x two columns (Optimise set / Held-out) animated with layout transitions; bottom timeline scrubber (orders processed / total) with speed 1x/5x/20x and "skip to end"; an "Evidence" tab and an "Assumptions" tab. All HUD text >= 18 px, contrast >= 7:1 for projectors. prefers-reduced-motion disables the intro dolly and cascade.
- Performance targets: 60 fps on Intel Iris Xe at dpr 1.25 in High; <= 14 static draw calls, 2 skinned meshes, 2 line draw calls, 3 post passes; r3f-perf 7.2.3 in dev only; no shadows on Low; frustum culling on; texture 2048 max.
wow_technical:
1) Warehouse graph (src/sim/layout.ts). Declared layout: 5 pick aisles x 2 sides x 10 bays = 100 slots (two blocks of 5 bays split by a middle cross-aisle); bay pitch 1.2 m, rack depth 1.0 m, aisle width 3.0 m, cross-aisle width 4.0 m, aisle pitch 5.0 m; front/middle/back cross-aisles; packing dock front-left at (-3, -2). Nodes = dock + 50 aisle-bay points + 15 cross-aisle junctions = 66; weighted edges (1.2 m along aisles, 4.0 m aisle-to-cross, 5.0 m between junctions). All-pairs Dijkstra (or Floyd-Warshall on 66 nodes) -> 101x101 Float32Array slot/dock distance matrix + predecessor table for path reconstruction. Both rack sides of a bay share the access node (stated).

2) Per-order routing (src/sim/route.ts). Stops = distinct access nodes of the order's slots. For n <= 11: exact Held-Karp bitmask DP O(n^2 2^n) starting and ending at the dock (11: ~250k ops). For n > 11: nearest-neighbour + 2-opt + Or-opt (max 200 passes). Also sShape() (traverse every aisle containing a pick end-to-end, Hall 1993) and largestGap() for an ablation table showing how much exact routing saves on the same layout. Tests: Held-Karp vs brute-force permutations for n <= 7 on a toy 2-aisle layout; hand-checked BFS distances.

3) Deterministic headless simulator (src/sim/simulate.ts). simulate(layout: Uint8Array slotOfSku[100], orders) -> {totalM, totalS, perOrder[{inv, m, s, routeNodes}]}; time = m / 1.2 + 10 s x lines. Pure, no Date.now, no Math.random. Used by: the Web Worker (scores all orders of a set in < 100 ms, measured and shown as a chip), the eval script, and the animation (which only plays back perOrder routes). This answers the judge probe "does the score come from the animation?" with "same function, worker runs it on all orders before the first frame".

4) Slotting opponents (src/sim/slotting.ts). Baseline (must-have): sort SKUs by picks desc, slots by matrix[dock][slot] asc, zip. SA: state = permutation; move = swap two SKUs; objective = simulate(...).totalM on the optimise set computed incrementally: invertedIndex[sku] = orders containing it (~40-120 each); a swap re-routes only orders touching i or j (cache per-order metres), so one move costs ~100-200 tiny Held-Karps (~0.3-0.8 ms). T0 = mean |delta| over 200 random probe swaps; geometric cooling alpha chosen so T reaches T0/200 at 30k iterations; Metropolis acceptance; mulberry32 seed shown in UI; runs in the worker with progress messages (iteration, T, best, accepted swaps for the cinema view). Expected (to be measured, not promised): baseline 25-40% below random original; SA a further 3-10% below baseline because it co-locates co-picked SKUs (affinity), which ABC/COI slotting cannot represent.

5) Evaluation protocol. Time split: invoices dated Nov 1-15 2011 = optimise set (SA and player tune on it, the heatmap shows it), Nov 16-30 = held-out. Report for Original (seeded random, seed 42), Baseline, SA, Player: total walking km and avg seconds/order on both sets; the delta in-sample vs held-out is printed side by side. Routing ablation on the Original layout: S-shape vs largest-gap vs exact. `npm run eval` (tsx eval/run-eval.ts) regenerates eval/results.md with git hash and date; the UI KPI card is produced by the same simulate() so README = app.

6) Stretch depth if time: order batching (cart holds k orders; Clarke-Wright-style savings merge on route-length deltas) and two pickers with aisle congestion (time-stepped 0.5 s; a picker entering an aisle segment occupied by the other waits; delay reported) — both measured by the same simulator so they add KPI rows, not claims.

Metric that proves it: the held-out table (km and s/order for four layouts), the SA-vs-baseline gap on held-out, the in-sample vs held-out shrinkage, and the routing-policy ablation — all reproducible by one command.
mvp_mapping:
M1 Pre-processing (prep/prep.py, pandas 3.0.6 + pyarrow 26.0.0, Python 3.12): read the HF parquet mirror of Online Retail II (1,067,371 rows), filter InvoiceDate in [2011-11-01, 2011-12-01); drop Invoice starting with "C" (count logged), drop Quantity <= 0 and Price <= 0 (counts logged), keep StockCode matching ^\d{5}[A-Za-z]{0,2}$ (drops POST, D, M, S, DOT, BANK CHARGES, CRUK, AMAZONFEE, ADJUST, gift_*; count logged); aggregate duplicate (Invoice, StockCode) lines; rank SKUs by number of pick lines; keep top 100; orders = invoices with >= 1 covered line (kept lines only); emit web/public/data/orders_2011-11.json = {meta:{source, licence, citation, month, rows_in_month, c_invoices_removed, nonproduct_removed, nonpositive_removed, lines_total, lines_covered, coverage_pct, orders_total, orders_kept, split_rule}, skus:[{code, desc, picks, qty}], orders:[{inv, ts, lines:[{code, qty}]}], split:{opt:[inv], test:[inv]}}. Shown in-app under Evidence; file < 500 KB. Satisfies "top ~100 products, how often each is picked, and the list of orders".

M2 3D twin replaying orders: grid warehouse with racks (6 rack rows x 10 bays x 3 levels), 5 aisles + 3 cross-aisles painted on the floor, a packing dock with hazard stripes and a "PACKING" label, one animated picker (Kenney GLB walk cycle + cart) that walks the graph shortest paths (never through racks; the drawn route proves it) to each slot in the routed order and back to the dock, with live metres and mm:ss counters driven by the same per-order numbers the worker scored; order ID and lines shown on screen; click any carton for its StockCode/description/pick count from the JSON.

M3 Game mode: Overview camera; click-to-swap (click carton, click destination; arc animation) as the primary interaction, drei <DragControls> drag-and-drop as the enhanced path; "Replay same orders" re-scores both sets in the worker and shows before/after total distance and pick time (Original vs You) plus the Ghost Race animation; "Baseline: fast movers nearest dock" button applies the automatic baseline and adds its row; the SA "AI opponent" is an extra row above and beyond the must-have. KPI card = the problem's optional metric table (total walking distance and average pick time per order for original, baseline and player layouts) on both the optimise and held-out sets.
stretch_goals: Rack-visit heatmap toggle: carton instanceColor switches from pick-frequency to visits recorded during the last replay; near-free once instancing exists (stretch bullet 3a)
Leaderboard of player layouts (localStorage, name + held-out km + s/order; fixed rows for Baseline and AI (SA)); shareable layout via base64 permutation in the URL hash (stretch bullet 3b)
Batch picking: cart capacity k = 3 orders, savings-based merge using the same simulate(); adds a measured KPI row 'Batched (k=3)' (stretch bullet 2)

Two pickers with aisle congestion: time-stepped replay (0.5 s), a picker waits at an aisle entrance while the segment is occupied; reports total wait seconds and throughput; both pickers rendered (stretch bullet 1)
Annealer cinema: accepted SA swaps visualised as flying cartons with the energy sparkline, temperature and seed on screen
Drag-and-drop with drei DragControls and slot snapping, in addition to click-to-swap
2D projector-friendly slot grid panel (SVG) mirroring the 3D heat colours and supporting the same swaps
Routing-policy switcher in the UI (exact DP / S-shape / largest gap) with the ablation row updating live
data_plan:
Dataset: Online Retail II, UCI Machine Learning Repository id 502, CC BY 4.0. Citation: Chen, D. (2019). Online Retail II [Dataset]. UCI Machine Learning Repository, https://doi.org/10.24432/C5CG6D (page: https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/502/online+retail+ii). Obtain: the UCI zip truncates from campus and fetch_ucirepo(id=502) returns data_url null (verified by the data scout), so use the verified Hugging Face parquet mirror of the same file: `curl -L -o prep/raw/online_retail_II.parquet "https://huggingface.co/datasets/vancevo/online-retail-ii/resolve/main/data/train-00000-of-00001.parquet"` (7.16 MB, 1,067,371 rows, columns Invoice, StockCode, Description, Quantity, InvoiceDate, Price, Customer_ID, Country). Fallbacks: CSV https://huggingface.co/datasets/attik/Online-Retail-II-UCI/resolve/main/online_retail_II.csv (94.85 MB) or Kaggle anonymous https://www.kaggle.com/api/v1/datasets/download/mashlyn/online-retail-ii-uci (15.2 MB zip). README attributes UCI as origin and names the mirror used; raw file is git-ignored, the download command is in data/README.md, the derived JSON is committed.

Subset: November 2011 (the busiest month; invoices dated 2011-11-01 to 2011-11-30). Cleaning rules with logged counts: remove cancellations (Invoice LIKE 'C%'), remove Quantity <= 0 and Price <= 0, keep only product StockCodes ^\d{5}[A-Za-z]{0,2}$, merge duplicate invoice-line pairs. Pick frequency = number of order lines (not units). Top-100 SKUs by lines. Orders = invoices restricted to covered lines (>= 1 line kept). Coverage = covered lines / all cleaned November lines, shown in the UI and README (expected 15-30%; state the measured figure, do not round up). Held-out: time split, Nov 1-15 = optimise set, Nov 16-30 = held-out test set; SA and the player tune on the optimise set only; leaderboard ranks on held-out. Original layout = seeded random permutation (mulberry32 seed 42) because the dataset has no layout; declared in README and UI. Walking speed 1.2 m/s and 10 s per pick line cited as typical order-picking parameters (de Koster, Le-Duc and Roodbergen 2007, Eur. J. Oper. Res. 182(2)); all layout dimensions are the team's design and stated. Assets: Kenney Mini Characters 1 (CC0, https://kenney.nl/assets/mini-characters-1) credited in README; fonts Space Grotesk and JetBrains Mono (OFL) self-hosted. Processing is pandas-only, runs in < 30 s, one command: `python -I prep/prep.py --in prep/raw/online_retail_II.parquet --month 2011-11 --top 100 --out web/public/data/orders_2011-11.json`.
architecture:
Everything runs in the judge's browser; the only server is a static CDN.

repo/
  prep/prep.py                      pandas -> web/public/data/orders_2011-11.json (committed, < 500 KB)
  data/README.md                    source, licence, download + preprocessing commands, counts
  web/ (Vite 8 + React 19 + TypeScript, Tailwind 4 via @tailwindcss/vite)
    src/sim/layout.ts               layout constants, node/edge builder, all-pairs Dijkstra, predecessor paths, slot world coordinates
    src/sim/route.ts                heldKarp, nnTwoOptOrOpt, sShape, largestGap
    src/sim/simulate.ts             pure simulate(layout, orders, policy) -> totals + per-order routes
    src/sim/slotting.ts             baselineFastMovers, annealSlots (incremental delta via inverted index), seeded PRNG
    src/workers/sim.worker.ts       messages: SCORE{layout,set} -> totals in ms; ANNEAL{seed,iters} -> progress stream + final layout
    src/store.ts                    zustand 5: data, layouts (original/baseline/sa/player), mode, replay cursor, quality, kpis
    src/scene/{Floor,Racks,Cartons,Lamps,Picker,GhostPicker,RouteLine,HeatTiles,CameraRig,Effects,Swaps}.tsx
    src/ui/{Hud,OrderCard,Counters,KpiCard,SlotPanel,Timeline,Leaderboard,Assumptions,Evidence,QualityToggle}.tsx
    public/data, public/models (Kenney GLB), public/fonts
  eval/run-eval.ts                  imports src/sim; writes eval/results.md (tables, git hash, date); `npm run eval`
  tests/*.test.ts                   vitest: BFS distances, Held-Karp vs brute force, simulate determinism, baseline ordering, SA monotone best
  README.md, DEV_LOG.md, .env.example (no secrets needed; documents VITE_PUBLIC_URL only), LICENSE (MIT), docs/architecture.md (Mermaid), docs/pitch.pptx, docs/demo/script.md

Data flow: JSON fetched once at load -> store -> worker scores Original on both sets before the first frame -> scene renders cartons by pick heat -> Replay plays perOrder routes (main thread, rAF) while counters sum the same per-order metres/seconds -> player swaps mutate layout.player -> worker re-scores both sets (< 100 ms) -> Ghost Race plays perOrder routes of old vs new side by side -> SA runs in the worker streaming progress/accepted swaps -> KPI card and Evidence tab read the same totals the eval script prints.

Compute: animation + rendering on the main thread (WebGL via three 0.186.1); scoring and SA in a dedicated Web Worker; nothing on a server. Deployment: Vercel (framework Vite, root web/, output dist/, hobby tier, static CDN, no functions) + Cloudflare Pages mirror from the same repo + `npm run preview` on the demo laptop as the last fallback. Build output ~1.3 MB gz (three ~0.6 MB), GLB ~0.3 MB, JSON ~80 KB gz; first load < 3 s on venue Wi-Fi, then fully offline-capable for the session. No env vars, no cookies, localStorage only for leaderboard/quality preference.
stack: typescript 5.x (pin at `npm view typescript version` during setup)
@react-three/drei@10.7.9 (Instances, Line, Text, CameraControls, useGLTF, useAnimations, DragControls, PerformanceMonitor)
vitest 3.x (pin at setup) + tsx for eval script
Assets: Kenney Mini Characters 1 (CC0) GLB; Space Grotesk + JetBrains Mono (OFL) self-hosted
Hosting: Vercel Hobby static + Cloudflare Pages mirror; no backend, no API keys
build_plan:
Branch per agent, merge to main hourly via fast-forward PRs (humans merge, commit messages conventional, order matters: data/eval commits before tune commits). Walking skeleton deployed to Vercel by 23:30 IST (a cube walking a hard-coded path with a counter) for the progress-review multiplier.

Agent A — Sim core + data (branch feat/sim, ~5 h, 22:00-03:00): prep.py with logged counts and meta (1 h); layout.ts graph + Dijkstra + predecessor paths + slot coordinates (1 h); route.ts Held-Karp/NN-2opt-Oropt/S-shape/largest-gap with vitest brute-force checks (1.5 h); simulate.ts + worker SCORE message + eval/run-eval.ts writing results.md (1 h); slotting.ts baseline + SA with incremental delta and ANNEAL progress stream (1 h, continues to 04:00 if needed). Deliverables: orders JSON committed by 00:00, eval table (Original/Baseline/SA, opt + held-out, ablation) by 03:30.

Agent B — 3D scene (branch feat/scene, ~6 h, 22:00-04:30): Vite+R3F scaffold, Floor canvas texture, Racks/Cartons/Lamps instancing with heat colours (2 h); Picker GLB + walk clip + cart + ghost clone, polyline follower, RouteLine self-draw, next-stop ring, HeatTiles (2 h); CameraRig modes + Effects + quality Auto/High/Low + PerformanceMonitor + dpr cap (1.5 h); swap/cascade tween system (0.5 h). Uses a stub orders JSON until A lands, then the real one.

Agent C — Game UI + state (branch feat/ui, ~5 h, 23:00-05:00): zustand store + data loader + worker bridge (1 h); HUD: OrderCard, Counters, Timeline/speed, mode tabs (1.5 h); KpiCard (4 rows x 2 sets) + Evidence + Assumptions tabs reading meta and eval numbers (1 h); click-to-swap selection logic, SlotPanel with affinity hints (co-pick counts and current distance), Baseline/Replay/Race/Anneal buttons wired to the worker (1.5 h).

Integration 05:00-07:00 (A+B+C with a human): real data in the scene, Ghost Race wiring (two route players sharing one clock), SA cinema throttle, projector pass (font sizes, contrast), determinism check (replay twice), laptop perf test on the oldest machine available, Lighthouse.

Agent D — Stretch, docs, deck (branch feat/stretch, ~4 h, 07:00-11:00, only after M1-M3 are green on the live URL): heatmap toggle + leaderboard + URL-share (1 h); batch picking and/or two-picker congestion with KPI rows (2 h; cut if perf or time slips); README (12 sections per judge checklist), docs/architecture.md Mermaid, DEV_LOG updates, python-pptx deck skeleton (1 h).

honesty_plan:
Numbers: every figure in the app, README, deck and posts is produced by the same simulate() through `npm run eval`, which writes eval/results.md with the git hash and timestamp; the KPI card reads the identical totals; no cached or hand-typed results. Expected magnitudes in this plan (baseline 25-40% below random, SA 3-10% below baseline) are labelled as expectations and replaced by measured values; if SA fails to beat the baseline on held-out, that row is published as is.

Held-out: time split Nov 1-15 (optimise) / Nov 16-30 (held-out); SA and the player only see optimise-set statistics (heatmap, affinity hints); the leaderboard and headline claim use held-out numbers; in-sample vs held-out shrinkage is printed side by side.

Declared assumptions (README + in-app Assumptions tab): original layout = seeded random (seed 42) because the data has no layout; layout geometry (5 aisles x 2 sides x 10 bays, 1.2 m bay pitch, 3 m aisles, 4 m cross-aisles, dock front-left); 1.2 m/s walking and 10 s per pick line with citation; both rack sides share an access node; forward-pick area only (top-100 SKUs, coverage % shown); invoices treated as orders; routing policy per order size; no vertical travel, no cart capacity, no congestion or batching unless the stretch row exists and is measured.

Watch-outs respected and shown: cancellations (C-invoices), non-positive quantities/prices and non-product StockCodes removed with counts in meta; walking strictly on the aisle graph with the path drawn on the floor; simple geometry with instancing and a quality toggle for average laptops. Data provenance: UCI Online Retail II (CC BY 4.0) with DOI, mirror named, raw file not committed, derived JSON committed; Kenney CC0 and OFL fonts credited.

Limitations stated in README, Evidence tab and deck: synthetic layout, single site/month, no real WMS pick logs, pick time constant, routing ignores cart capacity and aisle blockage (unless stretch), results specific to this SKU subset; AI tools declared (Claude Code agents wrote scaffolding under human review; each module has a named human owner who can explain it); .env.example present even though no secrets are used; no personal data (Customer_ID dropped in prep).
